newsitem.title: USA: INSTANT VIEW - U.S. stocks seen up after PPI.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW - U.S. stocks seen up after PPI.

text.p: U.S. stocks were seen opening higher on Wednesday after a lower-than-expected report on the April Producer Price Index, analysts said. Following are their comments:
ALAN ACKERMAN, SENIOR VP AND MARKET STRATEGIST, FAHNESTOCK AND CO:
-- "The Fed appears on an economic and political hotspot."

-- "Inflation numbers remain relatively benign. Any Fed rate hike may cause some damage to both market and business psychologies." He said he expected the stock market to react "positively" to the PPI report.

The Labor Department said the PPI fell 0.6 percent in April. Excluding food and energy, the index was down 0.1 percent. Economists had expected overall PPI to stay unchanged and the core rate was seen rising 0.1 percent.
LARRY WACHTEL, ANALYST AT PRUDENTIAL SECURITIES:
-- "It's a very friendly number to the bonds and of course bonds are the gatekeeper to the stocks."
-- "It throws into question what Fed will do next Tuesday" at the meeting of the rate-setting Federal Open Market Committee. "This again raises the debate to a new level."
PIERRE ELLIS, SENIOR ECONOMIST, PRIMARK DECISION ECONOMICS:
-- Called the data "very favorable, it's a relief. There is absolutely no sign of inflation."

-- The figures "should get a favorable reaction (from the stock market) but the extent of the favorable reaction should be limited. This might produce some forward movement but there won't be much forward movement until after the Fed has met."
The S&P 500 future was up 5.40 to 843.25.
The 30-year Treasury bond rose 19/32, its yield falling to 6.88 percent from Tuesday's close at 6.93 percent.
